managers.loreTitle: The Commissioner — The League’s Supreme Ruler
managers.loreText: He doesn’t manage a fantasy league; he governs a tiny sports dictatorship with a weekly controversy budget. If there’s a questionable rule, he’ll enforce it. If there’s no questionable rule, he’ll invent one—anything for the win. The constitution says “fair play”; the commissioner says, “Show me where.”

The Juice enters every season like he’s starring in a sports movie nobody else has seen. In this league’s cartoon universe, his daily juice-fueled roid rage turns every house visit into an unskippable boss fight. Visitors came to say hello; now they’re extras in his imaginary comeback movie. When his team loses, it’s bad coaching, bad luck, bad teammates—everybody’s at fault except the guy who drafted the team. All that horsepower, and the lineup still needs a jump-start.

He’s calm, quiet, and much too nice for this league. Then his team sneaks up and beats somebody who was already planning the victory speech. He doesn’t need to talk trash; his roster sends a brief, respectful notification that you lost.

managers.characterDescription: blue hair guy with skinny legs
managers.loreText: He’ll light the group chat on fire, toss in one last jab, then disappear like the witness protection program just called. Ben complains when anything doesn’t go his way: the lineup, the score, the weather—apparently the universe forgot to clear its decisions with him. Every inconvenience comes with a fresh threat to quit. He’s not leaving, though. He’s just making sure everyone knows he could.

managers.loreTitle: The Caveman — The Kings’ Unofficial Enforcer
managers.loreText: He loves the Kings, breaks things, and delivers banter with the self-awareness of a boulder rolling downhill. He was the commissioner’s second-in-command until he secretly helped Erik organize his bench. That wasn’t betrayal, he says. It was “UGG—help friend.”

managers.characterDescription: older guy in a dodgers hat
managers.loreTitle: IR BOB — The Dodgers’ Most Animated Fan
managers.loreText: IR BOB’s fictional front office has a revolving door for new coaches and an entire recruiting department for absolutely unhinged team moms. At this point the carpool needs its own general manager. He isn’t filing complaints with the Commissioner; he’s fully enlisted in Team Anti-Commish. If this league ever stages a coup, IR BOB already has the matching Dodgers cap.

Erik missed the opening days, set the team to auto, and let destiny take the wheel. Now his best friend is the caveman, his roster is a work in progress, and his draft strategy appears to involve bananas and hope. Somehow, the robot is still clocking in every week.

managers.characterDescription: young monkey or young guy in a jester hat
managers.loreTitle: The Young Monkey — The Self-Appointed GOAT
managers.loreText: He’s clueless about hockey, confused by fantasy, and somehow still has a take on every single thing. He stirs the chat, dishes it out, and sometimes the return fire is twice as bad as anything he started. Somehow every bad take, bad lineup and incoming roast is AI’s fault—as if a chatbot personally deleted his hockey career. The Young Monkey may not have a game plan, but he’s already picked the scapegoat.
